### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via business_unit (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9b400f6adb0d3a49e33a5ecebd90d67e418e467a` — the merge of head `d4179f207c73a6030e06be4a7230687387ec2e45` into base `63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9b400f6adb0d3a49e33a5ecebd90d67e418e467a && git checkout 9b400f6adb0d3a49e33a5ecebd90d67e418e467a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 d4179f207c73a6030e06be4a7230687387ec2e45 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7 && git merge --no-ff d4179f207c73a6030e06be4a7230687387ec2e45

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63db7240aae262a06fd61430fea84515c0928fa7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `03ff3585e9d0a441b386c6d544da32d3b7fd1f53`
Area: S2 · Fixes #33791 · ordinary ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md. No contract face: no `packages/spec/src`, no governed path, and no narrowing arm.

1. **Premise measured.** On the unchanged `origin/main` loader, with the stub corrected to serve the as-authored definition, the graph pins fail 3/11 and the runtime pins 5/31. The existing #33207 `owner_id: 'Zhang Wei'` case also goes red. That stub is exactly the mask the card names.
   - The ablation replaced the owner guard. It was rebuilt, and a dist preflight confirmed the marker was absent. The same cases went red, then the source was restored to blob == HEAD.
2. **Mechanism, read on the tree.** `seedReferenceGraphFields` adds `owner_id` to the graph only when two things hold: `resolveInjectedSystemColumns(definition).owner` says the column is injected, and the object does not declare `owner_id`.
   - The added definition is `OWNER_FIELD_DEF`, the same `sys_user` lookup that objectql's system-field pass registers (pinned equal in `injected-system-columns-parity.test.ts` on main). The injected owner therefore takes the declared-lookup path unchanged: unscoped with no organization, membership-scoped on an organization's load, and NULL plus "not a member" for a non-member.
   - A declared `owner_id` wins, whatever its type. The no-owner postures (`org`, `none`, `business_unit`, `managedBy`, `sys_*`, `systemFields: false`) are pinned unchanged.
3. **Clause-② no, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`: right.** No schema key, value or export moves, and `OWNER_FIELD_DEF` was already exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`. The new behaviour is the one the 18.5.0 changeset and `seed-data.mdx` (the `sys_user` target row) already promise. Dogfood is n/a because the PR has no `!` and no narrowing arm.
4. **Downstream.** I checked the local HotCRM clone. No seed sets a person name in `owner_id`. `objectstack.composition.ts` documents that ownership is left to the first-admin claim, and `forecast.seed.ts` leaves `owner_id` unset. The new NULL-plus-error answer therefore reaches no shipped seed. The `SeedLoaderService` consumers the body lists (objectql, cloud-connection install-local, cli parity) were run green.
5. **Tests.**
   - The fixture triage in `seed-loader-reference-carrier` and `seed-loader-implicit-reference-target` is right. Those fixtures are user-owned objects, so the new `owner_id` row is correct for them, and the assertions keep judging the declared carrier field.
   - `runtime/seed-loader.test.ts` now names both rows.
   - The non-member cases assert NULL plus the "not a member of organization" error on both `owner_id` and `rep`.
6. **Changeset.** Each sentence matches the diff, including "rewrites no stored row".
7. **Scope.** Two things in the Acceptance notes are left out, and that is right for this card's ruling:
   - The audit `*_by` and `owning_business_unit_id` lookups are injected too, but they are readonly and server-stamped.
   - The card's related observation is also out: on a walled boot, the organization-create replay runs before the founder's `sys_member` row is written.
   Neither is filed. The seat decides in the ACCEPT whether each gets a card or an accepted-deviation line.
8. **Check-runs on the head:** 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed or pending.

A clean `origin/main` merge whose PR patch-id equals this head's keeps this PASS (16:10Z rule). A head move that changes the patch needs a delta.

domain:server#5 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jUg7BKfRBcTPyMxbLh

Holding the re-queue. The second queue build, 43743119181, hit the same signature (`run-date.test.ts`, 2028-03-31, `Test timed out in 5000ms`). Head is now `d4179f207c73a6030e06be4a7230687387ec2e45` after a K=18 main merge; the 3-dot patch-id is unchanged at `9ad5f52564e2`, so review PASS 6898091549 still holds.

Why this is not this PR's failure (read from code, not run):
- `run-date.test.ts` imports only scenarios' own `src` (loader, prompts, run-date, score, truth). Its one cross-package import is `scenario-tags.ts`, which takes two pure functions (`standaloneActionOwnerKey` from objectql, `effectiveSharingModel` from plugin-sharing).
